precedence_contract: Later explicit authority, especially Part XLV and Appendices BO–BW, supersedes conflicting earlier boundary/category/axis/coordinate/limit/quality/proof/example/compiler statements. Explanations preserve historical source wording and flag supersession rather than deleting it.

coverage.note: First batch covers Appendices N–AC; continuing through the hypercategorical/hyperordinal revision and implementation rules.

parts.title: Appendix N — IH proof drills
parts.explanation: A proof-drill suite for inheritance/provenance reasoning. It exercises one- and multi-step IH projection, rejects the converse S→IH(S), separates IH(¬S) from ¬IH(S), preserves exact-order information, computes ordinal-valued stage-source IH depth, rejects IH distribution, and keeps PA irreducibility intact even after inheritance projection.
reader_cautions: Use projection to recover inherited content, but never invent inheritance from mere truth or ordinary entailment. The heading begins after residual Appendix M material on page 169.

parts.title: Appendix O — Sixty phenotype examples classified by epistemic status
parts.explanation: A large phenotype-example catalogue explicitly tagged by epistemic status: causal inference/possibility, causal deduction only under an adopted bridge law, logical deduction, or not licensed. It demonstrates that exact anatomy, fertility, stature, intelligence, personality, stereotypical appearance and precise hormone values are not forced by stage labels, while formal type/depth claims can be deductions.
reader_cautions: The examples are status-training, not a catalogue of canonized phenotypes. Some N.14–N.15 proof drills precede Appendix O on page 171.

parts.title: Appendix P — Canonical conformance tests
parts.explanation: A conformance checklist for documents, AI systems and future revisions. It tests PA irreducibility and negation scope, IH projection/nonconverse/nonflattening, PH scope and profile-membership discipline, exact SF1/SM1 and eight-conjunct SF2/SM2 forms, type/depth/temporal rules, phenotype underdetermination and rejection of deprecated forms.
reader_cautions: Passing these tests means conformance to this edition’s core; later-authoritative revisions still control any specifically superseded boundary/category/limit rules.

parts.title: Appendix Q — Canonical reference for direct implementation
parts.explanation: A compact implementation reference assembling typed syntax, current stage constructors, limit/transordinal conformance requirements, SIH category-lift rules, local nonflawhood rules, depth recursion, and the metaexpression/modal extension. It is designed for direct storage/parser use rather than narrative explanation.
reader_cautions: This is an implementation snapshot. The preface explicitly allows Part XLV / BO–BW to supersede conflicting compiler, category, coordinate and limit statements.

parts.title: Appendix R — Final layman’s memory map
parts.explanation: A lay memory map reducing HGL reading to recurring questions: what sits inside PA, where NOT scopes, what IH inherits, how successor stages inherit own predecessor and opposite non-state, what actually grows, what PH adds, and what stage does not determine about maturity/environment/concrete traits.
reader_cautions: The opening of page 176 still contains the tail of Appendix Q’s implementation extension before Appendix R begins.

parts.title: Appendix S — Final specialist checklist
parts.explanation: A specialist proof-audit checklist: type every operator, stop illegal NOT movement, PA/IH distribution or flattening, preserve provenance and depth, keep stage distinct from maturity, reject unlicensed phenotype/psychology claims, construct limit states explicitly, distinguish quality/address/depth types, and keep modal reasoning address-relative.
reader_cautions: The checklist includes later-added transordinal, quality and modal checks; treat it as an audit aid rather than a substitute for the underlying definitions.

parts.title: Appendix T — Formal stage-relative modal semantics
parts.explanation: A Kripke-style biological modal semantics indexed by stage/address. It defines female/male accessibility among Γ-valid phenotype realizations, factivity via inclusion of the actual valid realization, fixed-address normal modal K, narrowly typed necessitation, and rejects automatic S4/S5 properties or cross-address persistence.
reader_cautions: Necessitation is a proof rule for model-valid theorems, not the claim actual(p)→□p. Stage-modal strengthening across addresses is a biological modal-status change, not necessitation.

parts.title: Appendix U — Biological Metaexpressability proof catalogue
parts.explanation: A compact proof/countermodel catalogue showing global Γ governance can yield nonuniform local outputs; static Γ can coexist with changing phenotype; actuality implies possibility; necessity implies actuality; possibility need not be actual; same stage need not mean same phenotype; and same current phenotype need not identify stage.
reader_cautions: T.9–T.10 precede Appendix U on page 179. No cross-address monotonicity of accessible phenotype spaces is assumed.

parts.title: Appendix V — Layman meta-phenotype atlas
parts.explanation: A set of explanatory analogies for Γ: configuration architecture, game rules, grammar, compositional system, jurisdiction, hyperparameter, building code and network rules. Each analogy illustrates global rule-governance without identical local outputs.
reader_cautions: The source explicitly says the analogies are explanatory only and do not replace the formal definition of Γ.

parts.title: Appendix W — Modal deduction/inference decision table in prose
parts.explanation: An epistemic decision guide for modal phenotype claims. Deduction requires a current Γ definition, adopted modal semantics, explicit PH membership, IH projection, PA rule or explicit causal bridge; broader HGL inference and causal inference remain non-theorems; exact claims should be refused when the needed rule is absent.
reader_cautions: Do not promote plausible generative relations to deductions, or infer stage/PH/cross-stage modal persistence from visual similarity alone.

parts.title: Appendix X — Final conceptual statement: metaexpressive-modal edition
parts.explanation: A conceptual synthesis of the PA–IH–PH–Γ architecture: PA supplies irreducible developmental causation, IH provenance-preserving inheritance, PH whole-profile possession and Γ global stage-specific metaexpression whose modal space governs what phenotypes may, must or cannot express. Static Γ can govern changing ordinary woman/man biology.
reader_cautions: This is the metaexpressive-modal synthesis before the subsequent explicit macroscopic/outward correction and before later hypercategorical authority.

parts.title: Appendix Y — Formal macroscopic/outward modal semantics
parts.explanation: Formalizes the Macroscopic Manifestation Axiom across micro/physiological/macro/internal-macro/outward phenotype domains. Every valid stage requires some stage-governed macroscopic and outward manifestation, including constructed limit stages, while the stage→visible phenotype map can remain non-injective and plateaus can change visibly under static Γ.
reader_cautions: Mandatory manifestation does not imply a stage-unique visible marker, monotonic size, or visual discontinuity at a limit.

parts.title: Appendix Z — Forty macroscopic and outward phenotype examples by epistemic status
parts.explanation: A visual/macro phenotype example catalogue showing which gross-anatomical/outward possibilities are illustrative or causal-inference schemas, which modal patterns are structurally permitted, and that complete macro/outward silence at a valid Archstage is rejected by the manifestation axiom.
reader_cautions: Specific breast, genital, pelvic, facial, skeletal, body-contour and other examples remain examples unless an explicit mapping law canonizes them.

parts.title: Appendix AA — AI conformance tests for macroscopic/outward HGL
parts.explanation: AI-facing tests for the visual correction: reject fully silent Archstages, total-visibility claims, static-Γ→static-phenotype, visual stage identifiability, scalar “higher stage means larger trait” reasoning, and invalid modal implications; accept stage-governed gross anatomy, visual overlap and properly typed modal possibility/factivity rules.
reader_cautions: The appendix begins on the same page as Appendix Z; use heading boundaries when attributing individual test items.

parts.title: Appendix AB — Deduction, inference, and causal-status catalogue for the visual correction
parts.explanation: Classifies the visual correction’s claims into strict deductions, HGL logical inferences, causal deductions and causal inferences. The general axiom forces some macro/outward manifestation but not any exact single trait; exact visible results require explicit Γ/developmental causal laws.
reader_cautions: Do not upgrade “plausibly richer/high-stage unusual morphology” into a theorem; the source labels those as inference.

parts.title: Appendix AC — Final corrected conceptual statement: macroexpressive-modal edition
parts.explanation: The corrected macroexpressive synthesis: “meta” marks the rule-order, not invisibility. Every valid Archstage globally governs complete-body physical phenotype and necessarily has some stage-governed macroscopic anatomical and outward realization, while much additional novelty may remain microscopic, physiological, latent, temporal or counterfactual and exact gross anatomy remains underdetermined.
reader_cautions: The page also carries a later memory formula for the global five-coordinate Archaddress and explicitly says older descriptor machinery is embedded/decoded rather than an extra global coordinate.
